components.css: .ds-tile{position:relative;width:230px;aspect-ratio:460/215;border-radius:18px;overflow:hidden;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#19d3ee,#bfe9f5);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);box-shadow:0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25);filter:brightness(.9);transition:transform .32s cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1),box-shadow .25s}.ds-tile-chosen{filter:none;border-color:rgba(255,255,255,0.22);box-shadow:0 0 0 3px #4CB8F5,0 0 14px rgba(76,184,245,0.5),0 8px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.45)}.ds-tile:hover{transform:scale(1.03)}.ds-tile::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;height:22%;background:linear-gradient(transparent,rgba(0,0,0,0.55))}.ds-tile-badge{position:absolute;top:9px;left:9px;z-index:1;display:grid;place-items:center;width:26px;height:26px;border-radius:50%;background:rgba(0,0,0,0.55);color:#9DB0C3;font:800 13px/1 "SF Pro Rounded",ui-rounded,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-tile-name{position:absolute;inset:0;display:grid;place-items:center;font:800 34px/1 "SF Pro Rounded",ui-rounded,system-ui,sans-serif;color:#fff;text-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)}

narrative.overview:
Porthole is a round window onto a deep, calm room, and the light in that room is the game. The background is a dark slate gradient; the chosen game's own artwork runs behind the top bar and the page, softly blurred; one accent glows where the person's attention is. It should feel cinematic and console-like: big artwork, strong contrast between light and deep, everything reachable from a thumb or a D-pad.

The surfaces are tactile and confident. Controls are large capsules and rounded tiles that spring a little when pressed, a gradient on the main action (Play), and a glow ring that marks what is selected. Panels are see-through glass with hairline edges, so the picture and the glow show faintly through them. Nothing is flat, grey or utilitarian, and nothing shouts: the artwork does the talking and the interface is the calm frame around it.

The default scheme is Deep Sea. Other schemes (Aurora, Sunset, Ember, Orchid, Graphite, seasonal ones, or a colour the person picks) swap the slate and the two accent colours and nothing else, so every rule holds for all of them.
keyCharacteristics: The game's artwork sits behind the bar and the page, blurred lightly, with the text over it. (Binding.)
Type is rounded system type: SF Pro Rounded, heavy for titles. (Binding.)
Glass panels over a glowing deep background; the accent is the only light.
Large, tactile controls with spring press feedback; a glow ring marks selection.
Works by touch, controller and keyboard: the same screen, the same focus ring.
A plain, honest voice in labels ("Not yet tested", "Runs rough"), never hype.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: The accent is the only thing that glows. Selection, the main action and the active section use it; nothing else is lit.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and coral mean exactly "works", "partly" and "fails". They are never used for emphasis.

rules.name: The Shade-When-Light Rule
rules.body: Where a game's picture can be light, glass surfaces get darker (Shaded Glass), so words keep their contrast. Do not fix legibility by dimming the picture further.

rules.name: The Rounded Voice Rule
rules.body: Everything is set in the rounded family. A second typeface is never introduced.

rules.name: The Shouts-Are-Small Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is only for small spaced labels, never for titles or buttons.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Chosen Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat glass at rest; lift and glow appear on the chosen or focused item.

rules.name: The Picture Reaches Under Rule
rules.body: The artwork is drawn behind the top bar as well as the page, never starting at the bar's lower edge; the bar and the page read as one screen.

dos: Do draw the chosen game's artwork behind the top bar and the page, lightly blurred (about 2.5px) with the shade at the very top, so the bar and the page read as one screen.
Do set every piece of text in the rounded system family, heavy for game names and bold for buttons.
Do make glass surfaces darker (Shaded Glass) on screens over a picture that can be light.
Do use the accent for selection, the main action and the active section only.
Do make everything reachable by touch and by controller, with the same glow ring on whatever is selected.
Do keep labels plain and honest ("Not yet tested", "Runs rough").
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface or a sharp-cornered, flat utilitarian control.
Don't start a picture at the bar's lower edge or draw an opaque bar over it.
Don't use green, amber or coral for emphasis; they mean works, partly and fails.
Don't hide the artwork under opaque cards; panels stay see-through glass.
Don't fix a hard-to-read screen by dimming its picture further; shade the glass instead.
Don't put uppercase on titles or buttons.
